sections: Choose a direction, not a full circuit

Kanchipuram and Pulicat offer two very different ways to leave Chennai for a day. One is a city with temple traditions and a silk-weaving identity. The other is a lagoon landscape where the interest lies in water, birds and the life around the shore. They are alternatives, not nearby stops to combine casually. Start with the experience you want and the time you can spend travelling. If you mainly want shore temples and stone sculpture, the Mahabalipuram guide is a separate option. A good Chennai excursion does not need to claim all three directions in one day.
Kanchipuram: choose a small temple plan

Kanchipuram's temple history is extensive, which makes a shorter plan more useful than a promise to see everything. Choose one or two temples whose current access suits the group, leaving room to move through the city rather than rushing from gate to gate. Temple timings can include periods when a shrine is closed between services. Check current darshan arrangements and any entry restrictions. Dress for a place of worship, follow instructions about shoes and belongings, and ask before taking photographs. A famous temple name does not guarantee access to every area for every visitor.
A silk stop should be deliberate

If textiles are part of the reason for visiting Kanchipuram, allow a separate window for them. Ask about fibre, zari, weaving method and place of production rather than relying on a shop sign or a driver's description. A shop visit is not automatically a visit to a working loom. Tell the driver or guide if you do not want shopping stops. If you do want them, agree the purpose and time available. For a substantial saree purchase, inspect the actual piece, get the material description on the bill and settle finishing and exchange terms before paying.
Pulicat: look at the landscape without a guarantee

Pulicat Lake is a coastal lagoon across the Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh landscape. The Tamil Nadu tourism account highlights the migratory-bird season, but that is a reason to research timing, not a guarantee that flamingos will be close to the shore on your visit. Use binoculars if you have them, keep a respectful distance and avoid noise or feeding. Choose a local, permitted way to experience the water and confirm whether any proposed boat outing is operating with suitable safety equipment. Do not assume every shoreline offers public access or that a boat is available simply because a travel post showed one.

Arrange transport for the chosen destination and the actual stops, with a return plan and time for food. Kanchipuram's temple streets and Pulicat's wetland shores have different rhythms; neither benefits from being forced into an identical timed checklist. Check weather, road conditions and current local notices close to departure. Heat may shorten a walk, and rain or wind may change the lagoon outing. Leave the unnecessary extra stop off the itinerary. The day is better when you can pay attention to the place you selected and still return without haste.
Croc Bank: a reptile-conservation visit on the coast road

The Madras Crocodile Bank Trust and Centre for Herpetology describes its visitor site as a reptile zoo with guided tours and educational activities. It gives an East Coast Road outing a different purpose from a beach stop or the monuments at Mamallapuram. Check the current visitor arrangements and any separately booked activity before travelling. An animal attraction is not permission to touch or feed wildlife; follow the centre's instructions and give the visit time of its own.
Kovalam: a surfing enquiry rather than an assumed swim

Surf Turf lists a surf school, lessons and other water activities at Kovalam near Chennai. This is a concrete provider lead for a lesson, not evidence of a safe sea session on every date. Confirm the actual location, instructor, swimming requirements, equipment, weather decision and cancellation terms before booking. Do not confuse this Tamil Nadu coastal outing with Kerala's Kovalam. A cafe visit and a surf lesson are separate choices.
Choose one main purpose along the coast

A conservation visit, a surf lesson and a stone-monument visit can all be interesting, but they compete for the same travel and daylight. Choose the activity that matters most, then confirm its duration and leave a return margin. An optional nearby stop should remain optional if the sea, weather or opening arrangements change.
